title: Zoos & Aquariums: Family Days Out and Ways to Save
description: The best zoos, safari parks and aquariums for family days out in the UK, US and Europe, plus ways to save: memberships, rail 2FOR1 and kids-go-free rules.
h1: Zoos, safari parks and aquariums for families
intro: Penguins at feeding time, giraffes at eye level and sharks overhead. Zoos and aquariums are a day out every age enjoys. Here are the best, with Scout’s tips.

image.alt: Two giraffes standing side by side

blocks.title: Scout’s zoo verdict
blocks.text: Arrive early, when the animals are most active, and plan your route around feeding times and keeper talks. Aquariums are the perfect rainy-day backup.

items.title: Chester Zoo

image.alt: Two giraffes standing side by side

items.text: One of the UK’s biggest zoos, run by a conservation charity, with a huge site to explore. Expect a full day.
saves: Membership can pay off if you live nearby and visit a few times a year
items.scout: Wear comfy shoes and bring snacks: it’s a big site with lots of walking.

items.title: London Zoo

image.alt: A mother gorilla hugging her baby

items.text: The world’s oldest scientific zoo, run by the conservation charity ZSL, in Regent’s Park.
saves: Listed on the National Rail Days Out Guide in 2026 (you need valid National Rail tickets)
Combine with a free picnic in Regent’s Park
items.scout: The Days Out Guide offer needs paper or e-tickets from National Rail; Oyster and contactless don’t count.

items.title: Longleat

image.alt: A safari vehicle driving through dry bush

items.text: The UK’s first drive-through safari park outside Africa, plus a stately home, gardens and adventure play.
saves: Its Festival of Light (in winter) is a separate seasonal event: check dates
items.scout: Keep windows up where the signs say so: the monkeys love a car aerial!

items.title: Edinburgh Zoo

image.alt: A visitor watching a penguin swim past the glass

items.text: A hillside zoo run by the Royal Zoological Society of Scotland, famous for its penguins.
saves: Kids Pass has listed discounts here: check the app
items.scout: It’s hilly, so a sturdy buggy or a carrier for tiny ones makes life easier.

items.title: SEA LIFE aquariums
items.where: Across the UK, Europe and the US

image.alt: A toddler touching the glass of an aquarium tank

items.text: Merlin’s chain of aquariums, with rainy-day-friendly indoor visits of a couple of hours. Great for toddlers.
saves: UK SEA LIFE centres (except Blackpool on new passes) are included in Merlin Annual Passes
Short visits: pair with another nearby activity
items.scout: A perfect rainy-day rescue. Most visits take 1.5–2 hours, so you can still do lunch out.

items.title: San Diego Zoo

image.alt: Two giraffes standing side by side

items.text: One of the world’s best-known zoos, in Balboa Park, with a separate Safari Park in Escondido.
saves: Balboa Park around the zoo has free gardens and play areas
items.scout: Plan a whole day and use the bus tours to save little legs.

items.title: Monterey Bay Aquarium

image.alt: An adult and child looking into a large aquarium tank

items.text: A world-famous aquarium on Cannery Row, with sea otters, kelp forests and a giant open-ocean exhibit.
saves: Book timed tickets online at busy times
Pair with free coastal walks along Monterey Bay
items.scout: Check the feeding and talk times on arrival: the otter feeds are a must.

items.title: ZooParc de Beauval

image.alt: A cheetah standing on a rock

items.text: One of Europe’s best-known zoos, with giant pandas and a cable car over the park.
saves: Two-day tickets suit families: it’s a big park
items.scout: Book hotels early: the Loire Valley gets busy in summer.

sections.html:
• Book online: most zoos charge less online and use timed entry at busy times.
  • Memberships: a year’s membership can cost little more than two visits for local families.
  • Rail offers: some zoos appear on the Days Out Guide.
  • Gift Aid tickets: charity zoos often show a price with an optional donation first. The standard ticket is usually available too.
  • Reciprocal discounts: some zoo memberships give discounts at partner zoos. Check your membership’s benefits.

More in Scout’s zoo day out tips.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit a zoo?
faqs.a: First thing in the morning, when animals are more active and crowds are smaller. Check feeding and keeper talk times as soon as you arrive.

faqs.q: Is a zoo membership worth it?
faqs.a: If you live nearby and expect to visit more than twice a year, a membership often works out cheaper, and supports the zoo’s conservation work.
